page: Amazon Web Services c5d.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz. The instance is equipped with 144.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 1800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the c5d.18xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 66669.07 and a Passmark CPU score of 49974.67. Memory bandwidth is also a strong point, reaching 209.03 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 90.37 GB/sec for large-block uncached writes. Database operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by a strong Passmark database score of 22233.59 and 61.64 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. However, single-core performance and LLM text generation speeds are relatively weaker, with text generation for a medium 7B model limited to 7.25 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5d.18xlarge offers high compute density and fast local NVMe storage, making it a viable option for workloads requiring high-speed scratch space and intensive CPU processing without the overhead of network-attached storage. The instance is well-suited for high-performance web serving, batch processing, distributed analytics, and high-throughput database operations. It is less optimal for GPU-dependent workloads or large-scale LLM text generation due to the lack of hardware accelerators.
